headline: Neighbors already vouch for you. The hours just don't agree yet.
summary: Dump Run of Southern California is a local junk removal and hauling service working out of the El Cajon area, handling household and commercial cleanouts and yard cleanups, with same-day service and text-for-a-quote right on the website. Neighbors named it a Nextdoor Neighborhood Favorite in 2025, and recent neighbor posts recommend you by name, which is about the best recommendation a hauler can get. Your phone number is the same on the website and on Nextdoor, your Google listing is up with the website linked, and the site makes it clear what you haul and how to reach you. The biggest leftover is hours. Your website shows 8 to 6, Google shows 8 to 7 every day, and Nextdoor shows 8 to 8 every day, so a neighbor checking one place and calling later in the evening can get a different answer than they expected. Picking one set and using it on the site, Google and Nextdoor keeps callers from guessing. A few smaller touches would help too: the website names San Diego while Nextdoor names El Cajon, and the site only offers a contact form, so adding the Gmail address you already use on Nextdoor gives people one more easy way to reach you. Once those line up, the reputation you've built by word of mouth has a place to show up online.

signals.note: Your Google listing is up as Dump Run of Southern California, marked open, with your website linked. People searching junk removal can land on you. Your Nextdoor reputation is strong, so keeping the Google profile matched to the site and Nextdoor keeps that word of mouth easy to find.
signals.next: Keep the Google profile claimed and make sure the hours and main phone there match the site and Nextdoor. After any change, ask a handful of happy customers to leave a review.

signals.note: Your number, (213) 590-2738, is the same on your website and on Nextdoor, and the site also offers 855-855-DUMP and a text-for-a-quote option. Callers have no trouble reaching you, which is the door that matters most. The only thing to watch is keeping one main number in front.
signals.next: Keep (213) 590-2738 as the main number on Google so it matches Nextdoor and the site. You can list 855-855-DUMP as an additional number on the profile.

signals.note: Your website shows 8 to 6, Google shows 8 to 7 every day, and your Nextdoor page shows 8 to 8 every day. A customer who checks one and calls at seven in the evening may get a different answer than they expected.
signals.next: Decide which hours you really keep and use the same ones on the website, Nextdoor and Google. If you take later jobs by arrangement, add a short line saying so.

signals.note: The Google listing is live, so there's already a place on Maps for people to see your truck or a before-and-after cleanout. For junk removal, those photos do a lot of the selling, because people want to see that the crew is real and leaves a place tidy. They're also easy to collect on every job.
signals.next: Snap a before and after on your next few jobs, plus a clear photo of the truck, and add them to the Google profile. A fresh photo every couple of weeks keeps the listing looking active.

signals.note: dumprunofsocal.com explains your services clearly, shows both phone numbers and invites texts for quotes, which is great. It offers only a contact form for written messages and names San Diego rather than the East County towns you serve. Adding a town or two and an email gives both people and search engines a better picture.
signals.next: Add the Gmail address from your Nextdoor page to the site's contact section, and name El Cajon, La Mesa and the nearby towns you cover. Then send yourself a test message from the form to be sure it arrives.

signals.note: Your name and phone match on the website and Nextdoor, and Google is up too. The town and hours still don't: San Diego and 8 to 6 on the site, El Cajon and 8 to 8 on Nextdoor, and 8 to 7 on Google.
signals.next: Pick one town to lead with, one set of hours and one main number, and use them on the website, Nextdoor and Google. A quick side-by-side check after the change keeps them matched.
